[b]I give them 10 days[/b]

Belgarde has surrendered to the joint expeditionary forces, stated Eleonore, walking into Henris office.

That is good, replied Henri setting down the phone having just gotten off a call, Do you know who that was?

Eleonore nodded, No,

That was the duc of Thýven, he wants some military backing to knock out an SCSID installation in his region, he says that the people are ready to secede as soon as the duc of Knygta and Deyn gives them the green light, replied Henri.

Eleonore nodded once more, And why is Knygta and Deyn waiting?

They want Montfleur to send some protection into the White Sea, in case the regime decides to be funny, replied Henri, leaning back, How long do you think we would have to wait if we activated part of our reserve fleet and a few frigates for this? 

Eleonore thought for a few minutes, If we scrambled, a day or two, depending on what ships already are able to be piloted? 

Henri nodded, My biggest concern is the Rosenmarkket sub fleet, intel is unsure on their crews, Begren played hard with them apparently, kept them in line,

Eleonore, I can look into it sir, I doubt theyd have the capacity to raise their entire submarine fleet, 

I want airstrikes, on the major docks, the submarine docks, stated Henri bluntly.

The SAM systems on the Rosenmarkket coastline is dense and well, even battered it produced some force against the Wuloosyans, replied Eleonore.

Lets look then at our options, replied Henri, Use strikes as a last resort, can we get Wuloosya in on this? 

I can check, replied Eleonore.

Good, nodded Henri, pulling out his VicodinEle from a drawer and popping one into his mouth.

[b]August 10, 2028: The long decline[/b]
[b]An Address to the Nation by Haakon Strømm[/b]

My fellow citizens, 

The nation is stronger than ever before, the fascist powers that have attempted to take over Belgarde have only perceived the sight of victory. The traitors who gave the state to our enemy shall be sought out and done justice to! The Eternal Revolution is stable! Order shall be restored, I am the Consul of Order! I myself have won the war against the Montfleurois and the Wuloosyans! We will win! Order shall be restored!

And upon that glorious day when the enemies of Rosenmarkke are cast asunder! I shall seek out reforms like never before! We will raise the pensions of our soldiers! Increase spending on social services! Everything shall be done in the name of our people! We will defend the integrity of the state, the nation, the ideology of Strømmism!

[b]Crisis[/b]

Thýven has just announced their secession, sir, stated Eleonore as she rushed into the situation room where Henri had gathered his staff to discuss potential strikes against the Rosenmarkket navy.

Have they? asked Henri, I assume they are sending a delegate post haste then, replied Henri, referring to the invitations he had sent out to the various seceding regions to send delegates to discuss unification.

They have, uh, a Iosep Østens? replied Eleonore, as she checked her notes.

Ah, Iosef Broz Østens, a former member of the Council of 99, a very well-rounded man, smiled Henri with a gleam in his eye. 

Yes, him, replied Eleonore, What do we have for Knygta and Deyn? 

James Wellton, some local official, I couldnt figure it out, replied Henri dismissively, Not a well known figure,

I see, has Westmarkke made any calls recently? Asked Eleonore.

Yes, they have signalled their intent, Thýven intends to push them furtherdid you see the speech by Haakon? asked Henri.

Yes, it was driveling madness, replied Eleonore.

I still give this regime 9 days? Maybe less, I meanpeople are massing in the capital city, and the soldiers not loyal to the regime, they wont fire on their own citizens, replied Henri.

What is the situation with the strikes? asked Eleonore, sitting down to look at the map that had been pulled up.

We are looking at striking one of their older ships, the last Cold War  frigate they have, replied Henri.

I can sign off on this, replied Eleonore, Itll send a message, 

Ah, so now you want strikes, the other day you didnt! chortled Henri.

On the subs, I am against striking the subs, replied Eleonore.

Ah, well, waved Henri, The subs, we will be striking those too, we know they are uncrewed, unmanned, and frankly stuck in the dock. 

WHAT? asked Eleonore as General Charles Martel de Funes entered the room to give an operational report.

Sir, began the general, We are ready to commit to the strikes, our forces are ready to send in ground troops as soon as we get the all clear from our forces in Belgarde,

You may proceed, nodded Henri. The general saluted and went out of the room to give the final orders.

Henri, if this screws us, Ill began Eleonore before being cut off, Ill take the responsibilty, he smiled.

[b]The King Takes the Reigns[/b]

29 July, 2028

The King had been closely watching the situation regarding Montfleur and Rosenmarkke. He felt that he had to force his cabinet into taking act according to his will here, since he was the unifying political force in the country and the Commander-in-Chief of the Armed Forces. 

He saw this as the perfect opportunity to exert the NABs official opinion on the conflict and inflict a blow to Rosenmarkke, a threat to Montfleur, a fellow member of the NAB. Not only that, but the NAB itself could not afford a member nation to lose a military conflict, so the King knew this very well. Not too long ago, they had just rejected a membership application from another country for not being developed enough in that regard.

The King pressed the ringer at the end of his desk, and his personal secretary walked in, bowing low.

Do-yun, summon the Prime Minister please.

Certainly, sir. he said, bowing before turning around and going to complete the task the King had told him to do.

Within an hour, the Prime Minister was getting out of his car, where the King was waiting for him.

Prime Minister.

Your Majesty. the Prime Minister said, bowing.

As you know, Ive summoned you here to talk about Montfleur and its situation with Rosenmarkke. Follow me to the Audience Room. Could we get something for you? Perhaps a fruit punch, a tea, coffee?

I could go for a coffee, yes. Thank you, Sir.

The King also let Do-yun know to summon the Heads of the Army before he walked into the Audience Room, to give him and the Prime Minister just enough time in the meeting to go over their plan to convince the Heads of the Army to agree with them before they arrived.

The King and the Prime Minister were now in the Audience Room, with the doors closed and the guards out of the room, though they were still outside the door for security purposes.

"Prime Minister, the situation in Rosenmarkke seems to be negatively impacting the government there Strømm government. The secession movement there is growing at a rapid pace and they want to join with Montfleur, as you know."

"Yes."

"Of course, I couldn't help but wonder about international speculation regarding Montfleur and its neutrality with this conflict, seeing that Rosenmarkke could use this as a pretense to start a military conflict with Montfleur, knowing that Montfleur is bound to respond."

"My deepest apologies, Your Majesty." Do-yun said, walking into the room, bowing. We've just received word that Rosenmarkke has declared war on Montfleur."

"Good Heavens." the King responded. "Alright, Do-yun. Thanks for letting us know."

Do-yun bowed and left the room.

"Sir, what do you suggest we do?"

"Well, the reason I called you here today is for you to assist me in convincing the Heads of the Army to agree with our stance that Montfleur is not violating the NAB's neutrality policy in this conflict, on top of the fact that we have just heard that Rosenmarkke declared war first, not Montfleur. You do agree with this, don't you?"

The Prime Minister realized that he was being pressured by the King to respond favorably. He didn't disagree with the King, in fact, he agreed with him, but for a few seconds briefly reflected on the King's words, seeing as the King rarely pressured his ministers into agreeing with him.

"Yes, I do. How would we convince them, Sir? I don't think we'll have a problem with them, but it is according to expectation that we inform them of the matter as well I assume?"

"Well, we'll do to them as I have just done to you, Prime Minister." the King said, smiling.

"I'm sorry Sir, I don't understand."

"I nudged you into supporting my take on this."

The Prime Minister's face turned red. He knew he wasn't supposed to answer right away that he knew what the King meant, but he knew from the start that he was referencing his tone of voice about the issue. Nonetheless, he returned the smile and laughed nervously.

"Oh." the Prime Minister said, forcing some more nervously laughing. "I can do that, Sir. I do that to the Opposition all the time on universally supported topics."

At this, the King laughed.

"I bet you do. I'm going to make it so that General Kwon of the Air Force already agrees with me, speaking to him in a more direct way about the situation, seeing as he is my strongest supporter among their group, you already know this. You're going to build on this and speak to them in a tone similar to mine, just speak in a casual way like they are already in agreement with us, but engage in conversation with me too to make it sound like you are also being told this in the same way I am telling them before you back me up."

The King pressed another ringer at the end of the table next to him.

"Certainly, Sir."

Do-yun walked in again, bowing.

"The Chiefs of Staff of the Army, Navy and his Commandant of the Marine Corps, and Air Force, Sir."

"Thank you, Do-yun. Send them in."

The King and Prime Minister stood up, and the Heads of the Army walked in, all bowing.

"Gentlemen, please sit down." said the King, gesturing to the seats in front of him.

"The Prime Minister and I just had our weekly briefing." 

Thankfully, the King had this excuse as to why the Prime Minister was in the Audience Room, since it was their briefing day anyways.

"As you know, Rosenmarkke has a major secession movement happening in the country, and as you have just heard, Rosenmarkke has declared war on Montfleur. Seeing as Montfleur is a fellow member of the NAB, I feel that we should make an official statement on behalf of the NAB that Montfleur is not violating its our neutrality policy, particularly in the military aspect, seeing as Rosenmarkke is the one who first declared war and is historic Montfleurois territory."

"General Kwon, I'll start with you first, since you are the Chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff. What is your take on this?"

"Well,"

Again, the King's aide-de-camp walked into the room, bowing low.

"Your Majesty, Your Excellencies, we've just received word that the provinces of Knygta and Deyn have seceded from Rosenmarkke."

"Thank you, Do-yun." the King said, as Do-yun bowed and left the room.

"General, please continue."

"Yes, Sir. My take on this whole situation was magnified after hearing that Rosenmarkke declared war on Montfleur, and now even more so when I see that there is a chance for Rosenmarkke to fall. If there have been successful attempts to break away from Rosenmarkke, then we know that Montfleur has a chance at reunification as the dominant power between Rosenmarkke and itself. Rosenmarkke is Montfleur."

"Your Majesty, if I may say something regarding this?" the Prime Minister said, sounding like he was new to the conversation.

"Sure, go ahead."

"Generals, I feel that we can cooperate in this regard. We would like the announcement for our supporting of Montfleur in this conflict to come from the military, and then for us to back you up, seeing as we wouldn't want this to look like a political decision. We wouldn't want the opposition getting ideas..."

The Chief of Staff of the Army spoke up.

"Well, we wouldn't want to get involved in politics. We could say what we have to say militarily and then you could say what you have to say politically."

The King sensed a point of tension, not major, but enough to get his attention. So, he intervened to calm the situation.

"Leave that to me, General. The people need to hear from their King to confirm such a major decision, so I will address the nation and give the NAB's official stance on this issue after both of your press briefings. Why not say that the military stance of the NAB is that Montfleur is not the hostile military power and that it is acting purely in self-defense, in line with neutrality standards? As for you, Prime Minister, let's have you give the NAB's political stance: that the people of Rosenmarkke deserve to be free and that Rosenmarkke is rightful Montfleurois territory. Reiterate the message saying that Montfleur is acting purely in self-defense as well."

"I will make an official address to the nation stating Minhokae's thoughts on all of this and grant Montfleur permission to tap into the NAB's Equilibrium Development Bank, used in situations or circumstances where member nations of the NAB agree to send economic aid to other member nations in need, should they request it and their request be approved."

"Sir, when the military has its press conference, should we at the Navy also say something similar, or be in the audience to back General Kwon up?" asked the Chief of Staff of the Navy.

"Precisely my question." the Commandant of the Marine Corps said, relaxing in his chair and snapping his fingers at the Navy Chief of Staff. 

The King reached back and picked up a peanut which he threw to Commandant of the Marine Corps, as well as everyone else in the room.

"Everyone will give their usual press conference updates pertaining to their department. General Kwon will speak for the Armed Forces as a whole regarding the situation with Rosenmarkke and Montfleur." replied the King, calmly before standing up.

"Gentlemen, great to have you here today. Keep me in the loop." [/spoiler]

[nation]Montfleur[/nation][/quote]
[b]Press Conference[/b]

Upon direction from the Chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff of the Armed Forces, his spokesman began the press conference on the recent events in Montfleur and Minhokae's official view on it all while the other spokesmen of the Chiefs of Staff for their individual branches gave their usual update rundown, the same with the spokesman of the Commandant of the Marine Corps.

"Good afternoon, everyone."

"We have a lot to get to today, so let's make the most of our time. Recently, His Majesty the King met with the Prime Minister and the Chiefs of Staff of our Armed Forces, as well as the Commandant of the Marine Corps. After much review and discussion, it was concluded that Montfleur's actions regarding the conflict in Rosenmarkke are found to be IN LINE with the Charter of the NAB, and is NOT found to be in violation of our strict adherence to neutrality."

"Minhokae's official view on the conflict is that Rosenmarkke is historically a territory that belongs to the Kingdom of Montfleur. Rosenmarkke's existence is illegitimate, and as such, Montfleur is simply intervening to remove the threat of an illegitimate state, one of which has also declared war on Montfleur. The Kingdom of Minhokae condemns this inhumane act and offers our full economic support to Montfleur."

"We have spoken with the government of Eneas and have found that we are in full agreement in opening up the NAB's Equilibrium Development Bank to Montfleur for economic assistance during the course of this horrible war initiated by Rosenmarkke. We are a neutral bloc, but anyone, especially an illegitimate state, who attacks any of our member states will face consequences. Rosenmarkke, as we have seen, is already severely weakened as a result of its corrupt and inhumane attitude to its citizens and to Montfleur. Minhokae stands with Montfleur and its people."

"Thank you, and may God bring about peace in this conflict."

He then bowed and walked out of the room.
